title: Deterministic multi-GPU conductor for kernel routing and comm-hiding across tensor/pipeline boundaries
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a deterministic multi-GPU 'conductor' that coordinates kernel selection, attention kernel variants, and prefill/decode scheduling to maximize NCCL overlap with local compute and reduce tail latency across tensor- and pipeline-parallel deployments. The conductor is a lightweight orchestrator (per-model-serving job) that produces a token-level execution timeline and issues timed kernel/comm directives to runtime workers so that large collective ops (AllToAll/AllGather/ReduceScatter) are prefetched and overlapped with independent compute whenever possible.

Scope: mid-term feature for hosted & dedicated modes, opt-in per model-version. Not a full control-plane rewrite — adds a scheduling layer in the runtime's scheduler component and small deterministic state machine in the serving agent.

Why: Existing heuristics either (a) choose kernels per-layer without cross-layer visibility or (b) let NCCL calls block critical decode compute leading to request tail spikes during prefill->decode transition. A conductor enables explicit comm-hiding windows and determinism for reproducible perf investigations and safe rollout (can pin to deterministic schedules).
acceptance_criteria: Conductor can generate an execution timeline and send step boundaries to workers for models with tensor+pipeline parallelism
Measured median token latency does not regress; 95th percentile latency reduced by at least 15% on internal multigpu benchmark compared to baseline for long-context chat workloads
NCCL collectives overlap with non-blocking local compute in >=70% of tokens in the benchmark trace (measured via flame/gputrace)
Rollout into canary pool supported via runtime config flag and telemetry (no infra downtime)
notes: Design doc outlines deterministic timeline primitives: epoch, step, prefetch-window, post-comm slack
We will reuse existing kernel-selection registry; conductor emits hints (preferred kernel id, args) but workers can override for hardware mismatch with logged reason
Fallback policy: if NCCL timeout or partial failure occurs, workers revert to best-effort local-only execution and mark schedule as degraded
Telemetry: new trace tags (conductor_id, schedule_version, step_id) must be propagated through trace spans for postmortem analysis
comments: 2026-02-20 Maya Patel: Initial proposal uploaded. Primary risk: increased coupling between scheduler and runtime agents. Next: prototype timeline emitter in a forked runtime branch.

2026-02-28 Jordan Kim: POC ran on 8xA100 with a 4-stage pipeline; observed 12% throughput uplift and 22% 95th latency drop for a 32k prefills test using fused-MHA kernels + prefetched AllToAll. Attached microbench data to PR.

2026-03-03 QA: Found intermittent stalls when a single GPU had a straggler kernel (spot found in gputrace sampling). Hypothesis: conductor's fixed slack window too small for nondeterministic kernel queueing. Proposed change: adaptive slack per-step based on recent quantiles.

2026-03-06 Engineering review (PR feedback): - Add robust option to fall back to previous schedule if NCCL error count > threshold - Add metrics for 'comm_hidden_fraction' - Make kernel hints advisory, not mandatory.

2026-03-09 Infra: Blocker identified — NCCL alltoall on our 4-GPU VPC instances has a known perf cliff with driver X.Y.Z. Opened infra ticket ENG-17012 to upgrade drivers and validate. Can proceed with local dev testing but canary gated until driver fix.

2026-03-12 Jordan Kim: Implemented adaptive slack and advisory kernel hints. Bench run after driver upgrade (ENG-17012 resolved) shows comm_hidden_fraction = 76% across test traces; 95th latency improved 27% vs baseline. Pushed PR #3456 for initial review.
